findings.claim: `kmctl summary ack` writes a new front-matter field, `checked`, holding a date and a list of concepts. Invariant I4 and ADR 0009 say kmctl writes only OKF fields plus extension fields an ADR names, and that `handoff_key` is the only one. `okf.field` raises KeyError on any path not in ALLOWED_FIELDS, and tests/test_okf_fields.py fails on any key it doesn't know. The plan doesn't name `checked` (or its nested paths) as an I4 extension, doesn't amend I4's wording, and doesn't update ALLOWED_FIELDS or test_okf_fields to cover ack. The planned ADR needs to name it. Otherwise ack breaks an enforced invariant, or gets built some other way, such as reusing `verified`, which ADR 0023 forbids.

.okf/summary.md is a root concept, so review_due._concepts picks it up, and review_due lists it as `unverified` until a person runs `kmctl verify`. Ack doesn't count as a person's check, by design. So in every `kmctl init` repo the summary stays in `kmctl review due`, and in the briefing's 'N concepts due' count, after an edit or an ack. The plan's success test says an edit or ack 'clears it', but only the `concepts changed` reason clears. The plan must decide whether the summary is exempt from the unverified rule (and stale_after), or say that only the freshness reason clears. That choice decides what the tests and the briefing state line assert.
`checked` (checked.at, checked.against) is now named as the second I4 extension in the new decision, with I4's wording, ALLOWED_FIELDS and tests/test_okf_fields.py following.
The summary is now exempt from the unverified and stale_after reasons, so the concepts-changed rule is its only reason to be listed and an edit or ack clears it fully.

kmctl summary ack cannot clear the summary when it already holds checked with today's date and the same ids. It rewrites identical bytes, so .okf/summary.md has no working-tree change, the commit-order rule still lists the summary, and ack still prints 'checked ... against ...' as if it had done something. Repro: init and commit; new decision X, ack, commit everything (clear); append a line to X and commit; review due lists summary (X); ack prints 'checked ... against X'; git status shows nothing; review due still lists summary (X), and kmctl check still warns. Editing the same concept twice in a day is common (the plan measures about 10 concept changes a day), and for the rest of that day the only way out is a hand edit to the body. That breaks r4's fails_when ('the summary stays listed after ... ack'). The r4 tests never ack twice against the same ids on the same day.

ROUTING always says 'Start at .okf/summary.md', even when the bundle has no summary.md. That happens in every project made before this change that moves its pin to this release (ADR 0026) and has not run kmctl update yet: the briefing sends the agent to a missing file at every session start, while the CLAUDE.md block still says .okf/index.md. render already knows whether a summary exists (summary_behind is None when there is none), so it can fall back to .okf/index.md.

User docs and the package's rule now contradict the change. docs/tutorials/get-started-with-kmctl.md step 2 gives kmctl init's output without the 'created .okf/summary.md' line it now prints, and says index.md is where a reader starts. apm/claude/.apm/instructions/okf-bundle.instructions.md and apm/antigravity/.apm/instructions/okf-bundle.instructions.md, which this repo ships, say '## Start at the root index'. README.md's 'Working on kmctl' says to start at .okf/index.md.

ADR 0027's Consequences says kmctl update in an older bundle 'writes summary.md and warns until .okf/index.md links it'. kmctl update warns once. After that, kmctl check fails with 'error index .okf/summary.md not listed in .okf/index.md' until the user adds the line, and that error also fails the kmctl-check pre-commit hook and CI. Say that the check fails (as it does for the manifesto), and add a line to commands.md's init/update section, so a person who upgrades knows the one manual step.

findings.claim: ack rewrote identical bytes on a same-day re-ack, so it could not clear the summary.
the briefing pointed at a missing summary.
docs still said readers start at the index.
ADR 0027 and commands.md misdescribed kmctl update.

ADR 0011's Consequences still says the kept-file exceptions are the kmctl block and the first decision's index entry and log line. init now has another one: the root index entry and log line for a manifesto or summary it writes into a kept bundle. The 2026-10-18 Correction this change adds to ADR 0011 covers only the block's new start line and sixth duty, so the record does not say it changed. README.md:112 also still says init 'keeps any file that already exists'. Add the new exception to ADR 0011's Correction (pointing at ADR 0027), update its decisions/index.md amendment note, and qualify the README sentence.

When the kept .okf/log.md is not UTF-8 but the index is, init prints 'linked .okf/summary.md from .okf/index.md, with a line in .okf/log.md' and then a warning that it could not add the line to log.md. The two lines contradict each other. Drop the 'with a line in .okf/log.md' clause, or print it only when the log line was written.
